1.1 Keeping Left / Right

1.2 Right of Way
Right of Way Rules
• Vehicles on a main road have priority over vehicles entering from a minor road.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right generally has priority.
• Emergency vehicles (ambulance, fire, police) always have absolute right of way.
• Pedestrians on a marked zebra crossing have right of way over all vehicles.
• Yield to oncoming traffic when making a left turn (right-hand traffic countries).
1.3 General Conduct on the Road
• Always wear a seat belt — driver and all passengers.
• Do not drive against the flow of traffic (wrong-way driving).
• Keep headlights on during low visibility conditions and at night.
• Do not cross solid white or yellow centre lines.
• Obey road markings, signals, and the instructions of traffic police.

CHAPTER 4 Lane Discipline & Overtaking
Proper lane discipline is essential for predictable traffic flow. Erratic lane changing is one of the leading causes of
4.1 Lane Usage Rules
• Use the left lane (or right lane in right-hand traffic) for normal driving.
• Overtaking lanes (fast lanes) should only be used for overtaking — return promptly.
• Do not straddle lane markings or occupy more than one lane.
• Signal well in advance (at least 30 m) before changing lanes.
• Check mirrors and blind spots before every lane change.
• Heavy vehicles should always use the leftmost lane on multi-lane roads.
4.2 When Overtaking Is Allowed
• Only overtake when there is a clear, unbroken line of sight ahead.
• Do not overtake at pedestrian crossings, intersections, or railway crossings.
• Never overtake when a solid white/yellow centre line is painted on the road.
• Ensure the road ahead is clear for sufficient distance at your speed.
• Do not overtake if the vehicle ahead is signalling to turn.
4.3 Prohibited Overtaking Situations
Never Overtake Here
• On a hill crest or blind corner
• At level/railway crossings
• On a narrow bridge or tunnel
• When approaching a pedestrian crossing
• When visibility is less than 500 m
• In school zones or congested areas

CHAPTER 5 Parking Rules & Regulations
5.1 Where You May NOT Park
No-Parking Zones
• Within 5 m of an intersection or junction
• On or near a pedestrian crossing / zebra crossing
• In front of driveways, entrances, or gates
• On a footpath, cycle lane, or median strip
• Near fire hydrants (within 3–5 m)
• On a yellow / double yellow kerb line
• Near a bus stop or taxi stand
• In a disabled bay without a valid permit
• On a main road or highway (except emergencies)
5.2 Parking Best Practices
• Always apply the handbrake and remove the ignition key.
• Turn wheels toward the kerb on a downhill slope.
• Use hazard lights if making a brief emergency stop on the road.
• Park within marked bays — do not block adjacent vehicles.
• Never leave the engine running in a parked vehicle unattended.

CHAPTER 6 Pedestrian & Cyclist Rules
6.1 Pedestrian Rules
• Always use the footpath / pavement; if none, walk facing oncoming traffic.
• Cross only at designated zebra crossings, subways, or signal-controlled crossings.
• Make eye contact with drivers before stepping onto the road.
• Do not use a mobile phone while crossing the road.
• Wear bright or reflective clothing when walking near roads at night.
• Children must be accompanied by adults near busy roads.
6.2 Cyclist Rules
• Always wear a certified helmet.
• Ride in designated cycle lanes where available.
• Use hand signals for turning — left hand out for left, raised for right.
• Equip your bicycle with front white light and rear red reflector/light at night.
• Do not ride on motorways, expressways, or highways.
• Obey all traffic signals; cyclists are bound by the same rules as motorists.
• Ride single file on narrow roads; maximum two abreast on wide roads.

CHAPTER 7 Alcohol, Drugs & Distracted Driving
7.1 Drink Driving
Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is one of the most dangerous and most prosecuted traffic offences global
BAC Level Typical Effect Legal Status
Reduced coordination, slowed reactions Legal (most jurisdictions)
0.05 – 0.08% Impaired judgment & vision Illegal in many countries
0.08% and above Significant impairment Illegal everywhere
Required for commercial & learner drivers Zero Tolerance
I If in doubt — DO NOT drive. Use a designated driver or cab.
7.2 Distracted Driving
• It is illegal to hold or use a mobile phone while driving in most countries.
• Hands-free phone use is allowed but still increases accident risk — avoid if possible.
• Eating, adjusting the GPS, or interacting with passengers can be just as distracting.
• Looking away from the road for just 2 seconds at 60 km/h means travelling 33 m blind.
• Drowsy driving is as dangerous as drunk driving — stop and rest if fatigued.

CHAPTER 8 Vehicle Requirements & Documentation
8.1 Mandatory Documents
Document Details
Driving Licence Valid, appropriate class for the vehicle being driven.
Vehicle Registration RC book / certificate — must match the vehicle.
Insurance Certificate
Minimum third-party insurance (comprehensive preferred).
Pollution Certificate (PUC) Valid emission test certificate (where applicable).
Fitness Certificate
Required for commercial vehicles; renewed periodically.
Permit
Necessary for transport/commercial vehicles operating in specific zones.
8.2 Vehicle Safety Equipment
• Working headlights, taillights, brake lights, and indicators.
• Functional horn — must not be excessively loud.
• Rear-view mirrors on both sides.
• Windscreen wipers in working condition.
• Tyre tread depth must meet legal minimums (typically ≥ 1.6 mm).
• Emergency reflective triangles and first aid kit (recommended / mandatory in many regions).
• Fire extinguisher mandatory for commercial/heavy vehicles.

CHAPTER 9 Intersections, Roundabouts & Merging
9.1 Approaching Intersections
• Slow down and be prepared to stop at every intersection.
• Look left–right–left before proceeding even on a green light.
• Never block the intersection — only enter if you can clear it.
• Pedestrians stepping off the kerb must be given priority.
9.2 Roundabouts
• Vehicles already in the roundabout have priority; yield before entering.
• Travel anti-clockwise in left-hand traffic countries (clockwise in right-hand).
• Use the left lane for exiting at the first or second exit.
• Use the right lane for going more than halfway around.
• Signal left as you exit; signal right when entering only if staying on the roundabout.
9.3 Merging onto Highways
• Match the speed of highway traffic before merging.
• Yield to vehicles already on the main road.
• Use the acceleration / merge lane fully before joining traffic.
• Never stop on the merge lane unless traffic is completely jammed.

CHAPTER 10 Emergency Vehicles & Situations
10.1 Yielding to Emergency Vehicles
When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens active, you must yield immediately. Obstructing an emer
• Move to the left and stop as safely as possible.
• Do NOT block intersections — clear them first, then pull over.
• Do not follow an emergency vehicle closely.
• Once the emergency vehicle passes, check for other following units before moving.
10.2 Breakdowns & Accidents
• Move the vehicle to the shoulder or a safe area if possible.
• Switch on hazard warning lights immediately.
• Place reflective warning triangles 50–100 m behind the vehicle.
• Do not stand on the road — stay behind the crash barrier or on the verge.
• Call emergency services (100 / 112 in India, 999 UK, 911 USA).
• Do not move seriously injured persons unless there is an immediate danger (fire, flood).
• Exchange insurance and contact details in case of minor collisions.

CHAPTER 12 Road Safety Tips & Best Practices
Beyond following rules, developing good driving habits and a safety-first mindset is the ultimate protection on the road
Before You Drive
• Inspect tyre pressure, lights, and fuel level.
• Adjust mirrors and seat position properly.
• Ensure all passengers are buckled in, including rear seats.
• Plan your route — avoid fatigue-induced navigation distractions.
While Driving
• Stay calm — road rage significantly increases accident risk.
• Use turn signals for every lane change and turn.
• Scan the road 10–12 seconds ahead, not just the vehicle in front.
• Check mirrors every 5–8 seconds while moving.
• Never assume another driver will follow the rules.
In Adverse Conditions
• Rain: Reduce speed by at least 30%, increase following distance.
• Fog: Use fog lights; keep speed low and follow the road edge.
• Night: Use high beams only where no oncoming traffic; dim for oncoming vehicles.
• School zones: Maximum alert; children are unpredictable.
• Construction zones: Follow temporary signs; workers have priority.
For Two-Wheeler Riders
• Wear a full-face or ISI-certified helmet at all times.
• Wear protective gear — gloves, jacket, boots where possible.
• Do not ride between lanes (lane splitting) unless explicitly legal.
• Be extra cautious of opening car doors (the 'door zone').
